changes.reason: Rename the ordering contract for atomic current-child readback. The local pre-submission Current check remains; each readback and recheck now proves authority and child contents at one cut instead of surrounding a child read with separate Current calls. The result and ordering assertions remain.

Rename the stale-authority contract around atomic current-child cuts. It still rejects stale authority before submission and at readback; a change after a completed cut must be rejected by the next recheck. All three boundaries retain refusal and event-order assertions.

Add the authenticated native-scope variant of the existing packet-boundary scenario. It needs CAP_BPF/CAP_NET_ADMIN and private network/bpffs namespaces, so ordinary cargo test ignores it. The required local-kernel-lifecycle manifest explicitly executes it; the original local-store case and shared scenario assertions remain.

Add authenticated native-scope coverage of coordinated GTP-U/DSCP opening. The new case requires privileged private kernel namespaces and is explicitly executed by the required local-kernel-lifecycle manifest. The ordinary-test ignore does not remove the original local-store case or its shared assertions.

Add the native-scope adapter to the existing session ownership, undo, publication and backpressure scenario. Privileged private kernel namespaces require an ordinary-test ignore; the required local-kernel-lifecycle manifest executes the new case and retains its local-store counterpart.

Add native-scope coverage of cancellation-safe shutdown and reset ownership. It requires privileged private kernel namespaces and runs explicitly in the required local-kernel-lifecycle manifest. The original local-store case and the shared cancellation/drain assertions remain.

Add native-scope authority to the existing XFRM expiration/acquire/undo scenario. The required local-kernel-lifecycle manifest explicitly runs this privileged private-namespace case; it is ignored only by ordinary cargo test. The original local-store case and shared assertions remain.

Add native-scope coverage that rebuilding an authority adapter cannot reinstall a retired effect. Privileged private-namespace execution is owned by the required local-kernel-lifecycle manifest. The original local-store test and the shared consumption/reinstall assertions remain.

Add native-scope coverage to the existing XFRM partial-effect, panic, cancellation and lost-publication-reply scenario. This new privileged private-namespace case is explicitly run by the required local-kernel-lifecycle manifest. Its local-store counterpart and shared assertions remain.

Add the authenticated native-scope variant of the real-quorum XFRM publication/store-loss scenario. The required local-kernel-lifecycle manifest runs it with its necessary kernel privileges and private namespaces. The original local-store case and its scenario assertions remain.

Add native-scope coverage of unknown committed replies and stale-child refusal. The case requires kernel privileges/private namespaces and is explicitly included in the required local-kernel-lifecycle manifest. The original local-store test and its shared refusal assertions remain.

Add native-scope authority to the existing opening, interrupted containment removal and publication scenario, including native work-class checks. The required local-kernel-lifecycle manifest runs this privileged private-namespace case. The original local-store case and its shared assertions remain.

Denied operational events now omit per-event audit work. The former audit-record assertions are replaced by an empty audit sink assertion; authenticated hidden-event and blocked-audit regressions cover omission and independent authorization termination.

Subtree scalar content matching is now supported under RFC 6241 section 6.2.5. The replacement checks bounded tree retention without flattening; authenticated generated-service tests cover matching, authorization, masking and resource limits.

Split the ordinary i686 lane by Cargo test binary to avoid its 30-minute job timeout. The ordinary slice retains the library and its existing ten exact exclusions, which still run in contracts. The ordinary-integration slice runs every registered integration target via --test *, all session-net doctests, and the unchanged opc-protocol/opc-proto-gtpv2c command. Both ordinary slices and contracts remain required by the same i686 aggregate. The named inventory partitions exactly as 807 + 572 = 1379, with no missing, extra or duplicate tests; all three doctest targets, features, profiles and test-thread limits are retained.

Rename the snapshot-origin purge regression to describe physical prefix reclamation. The test now requires covered rows to be absent through export and cold catalog reopen, while preserving its payload, membership, snapshot, and lineage assertions.

Transfer misc library execution to the required rust-libraries matrix using the explicit --split-libraries precheck/plan mode. The logical coverage plan still owns every original command; live compiled-library inventories partition exact names across two required runners with identical workspace packages, features, profiles, ignored status and test-thread counts. Scope-payload and child-read contracts remain fresh serial processes before ordinary execution on library shard 0. Binary unit tests, examples, doctests and the heavy remainder stay on misc. The three full-bound proofs move to dedicated required native-log shards with unchanged O1 commands, input sizes and assertions. Planner regressions cover total/disjoint identity ownership, future siblings, wrong-profile and overlap mutations, real Cargo execution including test=false libraries, and missing workflow dependencies. Existing job budgets and all test deadlines are unchanged.

Pre-Vote and precise election evaluation prevent the stale survivor from consuming the next term. Replace the obsolete expected authority timeout with recovery through the unchanged 26-second helper. The replacement preserves divergent 12/13 log prefixes and checks both real Pre-Vote replies, the fresh survivor's one persisted vote, fresh local authority, and reconciliation of both survivors.

The precise election timer now recovers from the retained real split vote before the unchanged 26-second transition bound. Replace the obsolete leaderless-at-deadline checkpoint with actual split-term checks and recovery before the same bound. Normal-time setup can also collapse 100 ms ticker phases: replace the distinct-phase setup assertions with observed aligned tick registrations and distinct finite RNG samples that order two genuine inquiries, crossed persisted votes, and one automatic retry. The history, retention, snapshot, reconciliation and durable-vote assertions remain. The measured assertion count including repeated local-helper call paths changes from 163 to 133; simplified tick alignment removes repeated phase-adjustment calls as well as replacing their setup checks.

Replace post-write failover at the physical cap with the caller-deadline read contract. The unchanged three-second deadline and 100 ms physical cap now require a pending written B read beyond the physical cap, a typed deadline result, exactly one B read, no C receipt or post-deadline read, the same single mutation on A, and a retained journal row. No caller bound or mutation authority is increased.

Keep traversal after completed unavailable replies, then require the unanswered written A read to consume the remaining original three-second deadline without another voter round. The replacement checks exact B/C/A order and call counts, the unchanged single mutation on A, the typed deadline result and a retained journal row. Completed NotFound retry rounds remain covered separately; no caller bound is increased.

The static helper resolver attributes the local OpenVoter::status refusal assertion to those calls, so its count falls by two. All three explicit admitted, leader and applied-index assertions remain, along with the exact receipt check, original operation bound and poll interval.

Reuse one admitted ConsensusSessionStore status captured inside the existing exact-receipt wait instead of three independent status calls. The static helper resolver attributes the local OpenVoter::status refusal assertion to those calls, so its count falls by two. All three explicit admitted, leader and applied-index assertions remain, along with the exact receipt check, original operation bound and poll interval.

Remove the redundant admitted assertion after the bounded receipt loop already requires that same captured status to be admitted before it can exit. A missing admission still fails within the original 30-second bound, now naming the last store, receipt and status. Exact receipt-index, leader and readiness assertions remain; no timeout, poll interval or production behavior changes.

The four PCO rejection assertions moved to positive retention/ignore coverage for issue #1441 in new tests (issue payloads, request/response retention, nonzero instances, builder round-trip, framing). The negative test keeps its AMBR, bearer-context, instance-shape and malformed-cause assertions; only the PCO-specific local-helper assertions were removed because that behaviour intentionally stopped being a rejection.

Issue #1208 replaces the two immediate status reads (higher term, non-leader) with one bounded wait_for_status_for_test predicate that checks the same two conditions; the static helper resolver attributes one fewer assertion to the test. Openraft publishes the successor term and non-leader state from its own engine task, so a single immediate read could observe the pre-stepdown snapshot. Every original property and the existing RECOVERY_TIMEOUT bound are preserved; no timeout was raised and no assertion was weakened.

Forced-timeout diagnostics regression is marked #[ignore] because this target executes with the privileged GTP-U datapath lane (`--ignored --nocapture`), the only lane that runs it; the regression itself needs no privilege. It asserts the shared datapath timeout diagnostics render every required field (redirect delta, shared-peer iteration, measured counter/drop expected and observed values, tentative addresses, neighbour and route state) and only adds coverage.

Replace the ad-hoc redirect-IT timeout eprintln block (which called `ip -6 addr/neigh show` with an expect) with the shared DatapathTimeoutDiagnostics formatter. The timeout assertion and every behavioral assertion are unchanged; the removed diagnostic `expect` is now a failure-safe bounded renderer, so the static helper resolver attributes fewer assertions while failures report strictly more datapath state (redirect delta, shared-peer iteration, counter values, tentative addresses, neighbours, routes).

Issue #1188 replaces the shared DatapathTimeoutDiagnostics formatter with the measured redirect failure-path renderer. The two enabled tests in crates/opc-gtpu-dataplane/tests/ebpf_gtpu_privileged/measured_diagnostics.rs retain panic context, both shared-peer iterations, redirect delta, counter values, tentative addresses, neighbours, routes and payload-marker exclusions, and add command failures and unavailable reads. The hand-off consumer, VRF hand-off and reassembly waits returned to main's messages because they are outside the redirect-diagnostics scope; their behavioral assertions remain.

Issue #1262 keeps SecurityKey IE bytes in their zeroizing typed owner. In crates/opc-n3iwf-fixtures/tests/ngap_messages.rs, this test now compares every reference IE value directly, including id 94. The two deleted assertions checked the obsolete empty-key placeholder and cleared the expected key before comparison. Exact typed-field equality, canonical encoding and raw-preserving encoding remain; restoring the placeholder assertions would contradict intact key custody.

In crates/opc-persist/src/retained/tests.rs, removing the preliminary established-store reopen avoids changing SQLite headers between the preservation snapshot and the rejected request, explaining 47 -> 41 transitive assertions. Refusal and byte-identical files remain checked at every CRASH_STAGES boundary, followed by unconditional established-store reopen, original-request resume and final reopen. Both conflicting and original requests now use ResumeAuthority: the former NewAuthority meant provision-or-resume, while the current Provision/NewAuthority refuses existing state. The separate process-loss test also checks byte preservation after a fresh request is refused.

Issue #1114 uses a permanent authenticated intent/lock inode and explicit resume rather than abort/unlink recovery. Replacement resume_does_not_remove_a_concurrent_owners_admission_lock in crates/opc-persist/src/retained/tests.rs holds the real admission lock, requires InUse and exact artifact preservation, then releases the owner and requires successful resume.

In crates/opc-persist/src/retained/tests.rs, this test replaces separate old fault loops with all 19 PROVISION_STEPS. At every step it requires failure and checks mutation classification and named intent presence against the publication boundary. The three prepublication O_TMPFILE steps must additionally leave an empty directory. Both pre-effect and post-publication outcomes remain asserted; removing the duplicated pre-effect setup/helper calls accounts for 20 -> 14 static assertions.

Issue #1114 replaces intent deletion with permanent intent plus synchronized completion publication. Replacement process_loss_after_completion_leaves_an_established_reopenable_store in crates/opc-persist/src/retained/tests.rs crashes after record_synced, requires both witnesses, successful ordinary reopen, AlreadyExists for fresh provisioning and a second successful reopen. The obsolete intent_removed hook no longer represents a production boundary.

Issue #1114 removes intent-unlink recovery. In crates/opc-persist/src/retained/tests.rs, resume_preserves_foreign_intent_file_types checks refusal and continued existence of the foreign regular file, symlink entry and target. resume_rejects_writable_authenticated_intent_without_mutation separately uses a valid authenticated intent with mode 0o666 to require Rejected and byte-identical files, then requires successful resume of the same intent after chmod 0o600. The latter also requires rejection before admission lock acquisition, so a later permission check cannot mask removal of the initial writable-intent guard; the positive control observes lock acquisition.

The old successful replacement assertion violated issue #1114: unauthenticated/torn intent cannot authorize initialization or deletion. Replacement torn_first_intent_without_artifacts_is_preserved_and_refused in crates/opc-persist/src/retained/tests.rs requires failed resume and reopen, byte-identical artifacts and no database. provisioning_regressions::unverifiable_interrupted_intent_is_preserved additionally covers empty and truncated records.

Pure rename to create_bearer_retains_a_well_formed_nested_pco in crates/opc-proto-gtpv2c/tests/dedicated_bearer.rs, preserving the body and assertions. The name/comment no longer imply that Update Bearer shares its PCO receive grammar. Create Bearer PCO remains the cross-interface compatibility surface retained for issue #585, not an S2b-table applicability claim; issue #1441 corrects Update Bearer PCO handling.

TS 29.274 V19.6.0 tables 7.2.15/16 do not assign PCO to S2b Update Bearer senders. Replacement update_bearer_builders_reject_non_s2b_pco in crates/opc-proto-gtpv2c/tests/dedicated_bearer.rs checks request/response builder refusal at both scopes and retains a valid request round-trip. update_bearer_rejects_wrong_instances_and_invalid_nested_shapes restores all four strict projection checks; issue_1441_payloads_decode_and_preserve_bearer_policy checks canonical omission and exact raw preservation of received PCO.

TS 29.274 V19.6.0 clause 7.7.9 discards non-applicable receive IEs before value interpretation or singleton bookkeeping; retaining the first unexpected PCO was incorrect. Replacement update_bearer_duplicate_nested_pco_discards_all_occurrences in crates/opc-proto-gtpv2c/tests/dedicated_bearer.rs uses the same two distinct nested PCOs and requires both discarded, no duplicate diagnostic, retained EBI and TFT, and successful projection.

TS 29.274 V19.6.0 clause 7.7.9 and tables 7.2.15/16 require discarding non-S2b PCO. Replacement update_bearer_discards_non_s2b_pco_at_both_scopes in crates/opc-proto-gtpv2c/tests/dedicated_bearer.rs retains request/response fixtures and bearer-policy checks, but correctly requires zero retained top-level and nested PCOs. issue_1441_payloads_decode_and_preserve_bearer_policy separately checks canonical omission and exact raw preservation.

Issue #1262 prevents implicit cloning of key-bearing structures. In crates/opc-proto-ngap/tests/constructed.rs, each adversary is built directly from the same paging_drx IE instead of clone_pdu encode/decode helper calls. All seven invalid wrapper/message/IE cases still require canonical rejection and unchanged destination, and every case explicitly receives saved raw bytes and checks exact raw-preserving output. Removed clone_pdu setup expectations and its transitive decoder helpers explain both guard findings; no adversary or rejection assertion was removed.

Issue #1262 moves NGAP byte custody from the removed shared opc-protocol carrier into crates/opc-proto-ngap/src/sensitive.rs. Replacement sensitive::tests::drop_zeroizes_content_before_the_allocation_is_released: The same 32-byte nonzero input is checked before drop, then the exact allocation pointer, length and cleared flag are observed before release instead of aggregate counters.

Issue #1262 moves NGAP byte custody from the removed shared opc-protocol carrier into crates/opc-proto-ngap/src/sensitive.rs. Replacement sensitive::tests::empty_and_partially_zero_buffers_are_handled: The same empty and mixed-zero buffers are dropped; the replacement checks two observations, all cleared flags and the exact mixed allocation pointer/length.

Issue #1262 moves NGAP byte custody from the removed shared opc-protocol carrier into crates/opc-proto-ngap/src/sensitive.rs. The actual Zeroizing-owner constructor now has a 16-byte input/drop test with an exact pointer/length/cleared observation, stronger than the old length-only constructor check.

Issue #1262 moves NGAP byte custody from the removed shared opc-protocol carrier into crates/opc-proto-ngap/src/sensitive.rs. Replacement sensitive::tests::from_vec_adopts_the_allocation_and_clears_it_on_drop: The same 24-byte vector must retain its allocation pointer and length, then produce the exact cleared-before-release observation.

In crates/opc-sctp/tests/data_chunk.rs, all nine assert_same_message checks were inlined in this same test: payload, stream_id, ppid, order, assoc_id, notification, event, truncated and control_truncated. Issue #1262 restores bytes::Bytes payload compatibility using wiping ownership, so direct payload equality replaces as_slice equality. The guard flags the deleted helper signature even though every comparison and both admission paths remain.

Issue #1204 is not resolved by treating every StorageUnavailable refusal as transient. In crates/opc-session-store/src/consensus/store/voter_slot_tests.rs, both survivor and successor reopen paths again make one real open call and unwrap its result. Removing reopen_with_transient_wait and the global injected-error hook reduces transitive static count 321 -> 320; all snapshot, key-identity, replacement, joint-consensus, final-state and restart assertions remain. Real exclusion/release and incompatible-identity controls live in voter_slot_lifecycle_tests.rs.

Issue #1204 does not authorize blanket retries of unclassified StorageUnavailable errors; its root cause remains open. Replacement incompatible_reopen_preserves_the_retained_voter_identity in crates/opc-session-store/src/consensus/store/voter_slot_lifecycle_tests.rs: The old test only exercised mock return values of the deleted retry helper. The replacement opens real storage with an incompatible enrollment key, requires VoterIdentityReplacementRequired, then reopens the original identity and verifies its unchanged voter table.

Issue #1204 does not authorize blanket retries of unclassified StorageUnavailable errors; its root cause remains open. Replacement retained_store_owner_refuses_reopen_until_its_release in crates/opc-session-store/src/consensus/store/voter_slot_lifecycle_tests.rs: The old mock-success-after-three-attempts assertion only specified the deleted blanket retry helper. The replacement retains a real owner after shutdown, requires StorageUnavailable on a single reopen, releases the owner and requires a successful single reopen.
